```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("tidyverse"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("lme4"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("Hmisc"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("corrplot"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("emmeans"))

```

First I create a function giving the broad sense heritability and the number of genotypes of a given dataset

```{r}
#| echo: false

# Define the function
analyse_output <- function(data) {
  
  # Fit the model with a fixed formula
  mod_h2 <- lme4::lmer(larvae_total_number ~ (1 | genotype) + (1 | session), data = data)
  
  # Get the variance components
  estimates <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mod_h2))
  
  # Extract the relevant variance components
  genetic_variance <- estimates$vcov[1]
  residual_variance <- estimates$vcov[3]  # Adjust based on the placement of residual variance
  
  # Get the number of levels for the 'session' random effect
  nbE <- nlevels(data$session)
  
  # Calculate heritability (h2)
  h2 <- genetic_variance / (genetic_variance + (residual_variance / nbE))
  

  nlvl<-nlevels(data$genotype)
  
  nnotation<-nrow(data)
  # Return a list with heritability and variance components
  result <- list(
    heritability = h2,
    number_of_genotypes = nlvl,
    number_of_notation = nnotation)
  
  return(result)
  
  

}
# Define the function to process data and generate correlation plots
analyse_data_correlation <- function(data, group_cols, value_col, save_plot = FALSE, plot_filename = "correlation_plot.png") {
  
  # Step 1: Summarize duplicates by calculating the mean of the specified value column
  data_summarized <- data %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(group_cols))) %>%  # Group by the relevant columns (e.g., genotype, session)
    summarise(
      mean_value = mean(!!sym(value_col), na.rm = TRUE), # Calculate the mean for the specified value column
      .groups = "drop" # Remove grouping after summarizing
    )
  
  # Step 2: Pivot the summarized dataset to widen the data (one column per unique value in 'session' or other categorical column)
  data_wide <- data_summarized %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = group_cols[2],              # Use the second column in 'group_cols' to create new columns (e.g., session)
      values_from = mean_value                  # Fill new columns with the calculated mean values
    ) %>%
    select(-group_cols[1])  # Remove the first grouping column (e.g., genotype)
  
  # Step 3: Compute the correlation matrix between the session columns
  
  # Compute correlation coefficients and p-values using rcorr
  rest <- rcorr(as.matrix(data_wide), type = "pearson")
  
  # Create the correlation matrix for plotting
  M2 <- rest$r
  diag(M2) <- NA  # Set the diagonal of the correlation matrix to NA
  
  # Step 4: Generate the correlation plot
  corr_plot <- corrplot(M2,
                        title = 'Correlation between Sessions',
                        na.label = "NA",
                        type = "upper",
                        method = "square",
                        p.mat = rest$P,
                        sig.level = 0.05,
                        tl.cex = 1.2,
                        tl.srt = 90,
                        tl.col = "black",
                        addCoef.col = "black",
                        mar = c(10, 0, 1, 0))
  
  # If save_plot is TRUE, save the plot as an image
  if (save_plot) {
    # Save the plot as a PNG file (or any other format you prefer)
    ggsave(plot_filename, plot = corr_plot, width = 8, height = 6)
    cat("Plot saved as", plot_filename, "\n")
  }
  
  # Return the correlation plot
  return(corr_plot)
}
```

## Raw dataset

```{r}
data250pisum_00 <- read.csv("../../../../../01.data/2023_screen_specifics_251genotypes/02.aphis_fabae_on_faba_collection/aphis_fabae_fecundity_on_faba_collection_2024-04-02.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, sep = ",") %>%  mutate(genotype = as.factor(genotype)) %>% mutate(session = as.factor(session)) 

analyse_output(data = data250pisum_00)

```

Before filtering the dataset we have 251 genotypes

## Missing data

```{r}
data250pisum_01 <- data250pisum_00 %>% filter(!is.na(larvae_total_number))
data250pisum_01$genotype <- droplevels(data250pisum_01$genotype)
analyse_output(data = data250pisum_01)
# Call the function to generate and display the correlation plot
analyse_data_correlation(data250pisum_01, 
                         group_cols = c("genotype", "session"), 
                         value_col = "larvae_total_number")

```

Few genotypes did not germinates, therefore we only have 249 genotypes. Heritability is quite low, only 0.17

## Remove row with no adult alive

We chose to remove all data from plants on which no adult aphid was found. This desision was made to get rid of biais and only asses the reproduction ability of the aphid. When the adult aphid dies the number of larvae will drop but only because the adult stayed less longer on the plant and not because the plant was not suitable for the reproduction.

```{r}

data250pisum_02<- data250pisum_01 %>% filter(adult_alive != "0") #remove if no adult
data250pisum_02$genotype <- droplevels(data250pisum_02$genotype)
analyse_output(data = data250pisum_02)
# Call the function to generate and display the correlation plot
analyse_data_correlation(data250pisum_02, 
                         group_cols = c("genotype", "session"), 
                         value_col = "larvae_total_number")
qqnorm(data250pisum_02$larvae_total_number)
```

this filtering led to the loss of 1 genotype but increased broad sense heritability up to 0.36

```{r}

# Identify the indices of the top 3 highest values
top_3_indices <- order(data250pisum_02$larvae_total_number, decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]

# View the top 3 highest values
data250pisum_02[top_3_indices, ]

# Remove the rows with the top 3 highest values
data250pisum_03 <- data250pisum_02[-top_3_indices, ]


qqnorm(data250pisum_03$larvae_total_number)




```

## filtering of genotypes with less than 6 repetitions

Now the question is :should we filter genotypes for which we have less than\
x repetition. When we selected the genotypes to keep for the metabolomic and transcriptomic analysis, it made sense to select only genotypes that we\
observed at least x times to unsure that we select a genotype stable across\
observations. with the folowing code:

```{r}
dfb <- data.frame(Column1 = character(), Column2 = character(), Column3 = character())

for (i in 1:12) {
  data <- data250pisum_03 %>%
    group_by(genotype) %>%           # Group by genotype
    filter(n() >= i) %>%             # Keep only groups with i or more repetitions
    ungroup() 
  data$genotype <- droplevels(data$genotype)
  nlvl<-nlevels(data$genotype)
  
  
  # Fit the model with a fixed formula
  mod_h2 <- lmer(larvae_total_number ~ (1 | genotype) + (1 | session), data = data)
  
  # Get the variance components
  estimates <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mod_h2))
  
  # Extract the relevant variance components
  genetic_variance <- estimates$vcov[1]
  residual_variance <- estimates$vcov[3]  # Adjust based on the placement of residual variance
  
  # Get the number of levels for the 'session' random effect
  nbE <- nlevels(data$session)
  
  # Calculate heritability (h2)
  h2 <- genetic_variance / (genetic_variance + (residual_variance / nbE))
  
  nnotation<-nrow(data)
  
  df <- data.frame(Nrep = i, Ngen = nlvl, H2 = h2, Nob = nnotation)
  dfb<-rbind(df, dfb)
}
plot(Nrep~Ngen, data =dfb)

plot(Nrep~H2, data =dfb)

plot(Nrep~Nob, data = dfb)
plot(Ngen~Nob, data = dfb)

```

based on these results it seems appropriate to use a \>= 5 threshold

```{r}


data250pisum_04 <- data250pisum_03 %>%
  group_by(genotype) %>%           # Group by genotype
  filter(n() >= 5) %>%             # Keep only groups with 6 or more repetitions
  ungroup()  
data250pisum_04$genotype <- droplevels(data250pisum_04$genotype)
analyse_output(data = data250pisum_04)
# Call the function to generate and display the correlation plot
analyse_data_correlation(data250pisum_04, 
                         group_cols = c("genotype", "session"), 
                         value_col = "larvae_total_number")
qqnorm(data250pisum_04$larvae_total_number)

```
broad sense heritability our final dataset is 0.277, the dataset contain 204 
genotype for a total of 1716 observation.
